answer: Participants stake a bonded deposit at the harbor registry to earn a verified identity, and each epoch they must solve a fresh proof-of-work tied to their reputation history. Sybils splitting into many fake identities must post the same deposit per identity and burn compute on every challenge, so costs scale linearly while honest agents amortize one stake across real work. Attackers who mass-register identities drain funds like meltwater from a glacier, slow and visible, while honest peers flow like an ocean current, cheap to sustain and easy to audit.
